items.title: Trump cuts India tariffs to 18% after Modi pledges to halt Russian oil

featured_image.name: India gets friendship discount on Trump tariffs

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Monday that the United States and India have reached an immediate trade deal following a phone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, lowering reciprocal tariffs from 25% to 18%. Under the agreement, India committed to stop buying Russian oil and purchase over $500 billion in US energy, technology, agricultural, and other products.[1][2]

The breakthrough marks a potential turning point in bilateral relations that had grown strained over the past year, with the US imposing steep 50% tariffs on Indian exports—among the highest applied to any country—in August 2025.[3][4]

items.title: US-Iran nuclear talks planned for Friday in Istanbul

featured_image.name: Steve Witkoff is involved in Middle East, Russia-Ukraine ...

items.description:
Turkey, Qatar, and Egypt are working to arrange urgent diplomatic talks between White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with a meeting planned for Friday in Istanbul, as escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran raise fears of a broader regional conflict.[1][2]

The diplomatic push comes as Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei warned Sunday that any U.S. attack would not remain limited. "The Americans should know that if they start a war, this time it will be a regional war," Khamenei said during a public address in Tehran. His comments followed the deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group to the Arabian Sea, which President Donald Trump has characterized as a "massive armada".[3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: QatarEnergy CEO says AI demand may flip LNG glut to shortage

featured_image.name: Qatar's North Field East gas expansion to begin output in mid-2026

items.description:
Rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and data centers could flip the global liquefied natural gas market from projected oversupply to shortage by the end of the decade, QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi warned at the opening of the LNG2026 conference in Doha on Monday.

"We always thought the market would have some kind of oversupply between 2025-2030 and beyond 2030 you will have a shortage," al-Kaabi said, adding that demand expectations have increased "mainly due to AI and data center requirements, which are sustained power requirements as a baseload."[1][2][3]

The warning comes as a record wave of LNG supply begins flowing from major projects in the United States and Qatar between 2026 and 2029, which had raised concerns among analysts about a supply glut that could depress prices. Projects like Golden Pass LNG on the U.S. Gulf Coast and Qatar's North Field Expansion are expected to contribute sizable new volumes.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: Pakistan says forces killed 145 militants in Balochistan

featured_image.name: Nearly 150 militants killed in 40-hour battle after deadly attacks in Pakistan

items.description:
Pakistan's security forces killed 145 militants over a 40-hour period following a wave of coordinated attacks across the southwestern province of Balochistan, marking one of the deadliest flare-ups in the region's decades-long separatist insurgency.

The violence, which erupted on Saturday across more than a dozen locations, left 17 law enforcement personnel and 31 civilians dead, according to Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, who addressed reporters in the provincial capital Quetta on Sunday.[1][2][3]

"We managed to kill 145 terrorists in 40 hours," Bugti said, describing the toll as the highest militant casualties in such a short span since Pakistan began its counterterrorism campaign. "The bodies of these 145 killed terrorists are in our custody, and some of them are Afghan nationals."[4][5][6]

items.title: Trump launches $12B critical minerals stockpile to counter China

featured_image.name: Trump plans to stockpile deep-sea metals to counter China ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump is set to launch Project Vault, a $12 billion initiative aimed at establishing a first-of-its-kind strategic critical minerals stockpile for the private sector, according to Bloomberg. The venture combines $1.67 billion in private capital with a $10 billion loan from the US Export-Import Bank to procure and store minerals for automakers, technology firms, and other manufacturers reliant on rare earths and other metals.[1][2][3]

The initiative represents the Trump administration's most aggressive effort yet to insulate American manufacturers from supply shocks and reduce reliance on Chinese-controlled supply chains. Details of the program were described by senior administration officials, though specifics about which minerals will be prioritized and where they will be stored have not been disclosed.[1]

items.title: MIT's AI model suggests recipes for making new materials

featured_image.name: AI materials discovery now needs to move into the real world

items.description:
MIT researchers have developed an AI model called DiffSyn that can suggest promising synthesis routes for complex materials, addressing one of the most time-consuming bottlenecks in materials science. The tool, described in a paper published today in Nature Computational Science, demonstrated state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting pathways for creating zeolites, a class of materials with applications in catalysis, absorption, and ion exchange processes.[1][2]

"To use an analogy, we know what kind of cake we want to make, but right now we don't know how to bake the cake," said lead author Elton Pan, a PhD candidate in MIT's Department of Materials Science and Engineering. "Materials synthesis is currently done through domain expertise and trial and error."[2][1]

items.title: European stocks tumble as metals selloff and oil slump hit markets

featured_image.name: European shares fall as commodities-linked stocks slide - Reuters

items.description:
The pan-European Stoxx 600 declined Monday as a global selloff in precious metals and a sharp drop in oil prices sent mining and energy stocks tumbling, while investors reassessed risk assets following President Donald Trump's nomination of Kevin Warsh as the next Federal Reserve chair.

The Stoxx 600 fell 0.4% in early trading, with the basic resources sector on track for its biggest daily decline since July 2025, dropping more than 2%. European energy stocks also slid, falling nearly 5% as oil prices tumbled on easing U.S.-Iran tensions.[1][2][3][4][5]
